ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three adjacent squares. Square III is on the left, larger; Square I is attached to the upper half of the right side of Square III; Square II is attached to the lower half of the right side of Square III. In the figure, the upper side of Square III is aligned with the upper side of Square I, the lower side of Square I is aligned with the upper side of Square II, and the lower side of Square II is aligned with the lower side of Square III. Therefore, the side length of Square III is equal to the side length of Square I plus the side length of Square II. Reasoning: The perimeter of Square I is 12, so the side length is 12 ÷ 4 = 3. The perimeter of Square II is 24, so the side length is 24 ÷ 4 = 6. The side length of Square III is 3 + 6 = 9, so the perimeter of Square III is 4 × 9 = 36.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as three adjacent squares: square III is on the left, square I is attached to the upper part of III's right side, and square II is attached to the lower part of III's right side. method.method_draft: Use the visual alignment to set up a perimeter relation directly. In the figure, the full height of square III is exactly the combined heights of square I and square II because I sits above II along III's right edge. Since the figures are squares, each height is also the side length, and each perimeter is four times that height. Thus the perimeter of III must be four times the combined height of I and II, which equals the sum of their perimeters: P_III = P_I + P_II = 12 + 24 = 36.
